tasks.short: Compare nanomaterial performance or environmental impact

steps.what: Check comparable nanomaterial measurements and size, shape or organization descriptors
inputs: existing actual laboratory measurements with sample identifiers, units and methods
measured size, shape or organization descriptors
outputs: checked comparison dataset with missing and incompatible measurements flagged

steps.what: Calculate comparable performance or impact summaries grouped by nanoparticle characteristics
inputs: checked comparison dataset with missing and incompatible measurements flagged
engineer-approved comparison method
outputs: reproducible comparison tables, plots and uncertainty summaries

steps.what: Interpret the performance or environmental-impact differences and alternative explanations
inputs: reproducible comparison tables, plots and uncertainty summaries
actual measurement methods and study limitations
outputs: human-authored comparison conclusions and explicit limits

steps.what: Assemble the nanomaterial comparison report with linked plots and actual conclusions
inputs: human-authored comparison conclusions and explicit limits
reproducible comparison tables, plots and uncertainty summaries

steps.what: Approve the completed report after checking calculations, comparability and meaning against sources
inputs: complete nanomaterial comparison report
checked comparison dataset with missing and incompatible measurements flagged

steps.what: Save the approved comparison report in the study record
inputs: approved final nanomaterial comparison report

tasks.design: Configure sample-linked comparison views in {DATA_PLATFORM} from the laboratory system {OPS_SYSTEM}, and reuse validated calculations in {SPREADSHEET}. A template in {DOCS} assembles checked plots and human-written conclusions; the technician decides whether measurements can support a comparison.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated unit checks, sample grouping, calculations and plot formatting can surround the scientific comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory exports and reusable analysis templates can carry identifiers, units and approved calculations through a report.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding, differing measurement conditions and uncertain exposure pathways make causal interpretation difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises when apparent differences reflect measurement conditions rather than nanomaterial properties.

ambition.what: Repeat the approved comparison when another measured sample batch becomes available.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1–4 for laboratory records and engineer consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory data exports and reusable scientific-analysis templates can validate units, group measured samples and regenerate comparison plots.

assumptions: Shares and savings are provisional scenario inputs, not measured baselines or claims about a particular laboratory.

Actual measurements, sample identifiers, descriptors, units and methods already exist in laboratory records. New measurement work is not free or replaced; if missing, obtain and count it before using this scenario.
The engineer approves the comparison method; the technician checks data and retains interpretation. No model predicts missing environmental impact values.
Native export and analysis templates are configured first. The same-system save takes approximately no time today and has no saving.
Performance and environmental-impact comparisons may use different data and methods; this is one comparison workflow, not a sum of two studies.
research_questions: Which unit, grouping and report-formatting work remains after native configuration?

already_counted.description: Check the complete comparison and its source support

incremental.description: Maintain sample mappings, validated calculations and report templates

approvals.approved_version: approved final nanomaterial comparison report; changes return to s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 10 data-check preparation hours +17.5 calculation/plot hours +4 report-assembly hours =31.5. Three upkeep hours give central net 28.5%; 6.5 additional hours resolving incompatible methods give high 22%. Low zero for already configured analysis or unusable source data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze environmental impact across a nanomaterial life cycle

steps.what: Define the life-cycle analysis scope, functional unit and material-specific assumptions with engineering guidance
inputs: actual nanomaterial or nano-enabled product design
engineer's analysis requirements
outputs: approved analysis scope and explicitly bounded assumptions

steps.what: Build and check the life-cycle inventory from actual material, energy, transport and disposal records
inputs: existing actual process material and energy records
documented supplier and transport data
documented disposal scenarios with source and uncertainty
approved analysis scope and explicitly bounded assumptions
outputs: checked life-cycle inventory with explicit gaps and provenance

steps.what: Run the approved life-cycle calculations and documented sensitivity scenarios
inputs: checked life-cycle inventory with explicit gaps and provenance
approved assessment method and versioned impact factors
outputs: reproducible impact calculations and sensitivity results

steps.what: Interpret environmental impact results and write the limitations of nanoscale release and fate assumptions
inputs: reproducible impact calculations and sensitivity results
checked life-cycle inventory with explicit gaps and provenance
outputs: human-authored impact interpretation and unresolved limitations

steps.what: Prepare the life-cycle report from actual results, source assumptions and human interpretation
inputs: human-authored impact interpretation and unresolved limitations
reproducible impact calculations and sensitivity results
approved analysis scope and explicitly bounded assumptions

steps.what: Check and approve the completed analysis report including source gaps and unsupported conclusions
inputs: complete life-cycle analysis report
checked life-cycle inventory with explicit gaps and provenance

steps.what: Save the approved life-cycle report in the engineering study record
inputs: approved final life-cycle analysis report

tasks.design: Reuse native exports from {ERP} into a checked inventory in {DATA_PLATFORM}, adding a deterministic mapping only where native import is insufficient. Configure the existing life-cycle assessment tool {OTHER} and report template in {DOCS}; the technician retains scope choices and interpretation of uncertain nanomaterial impacts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory field mapping, repeated scenario calculation and report assembly can consume effort around assessment judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned inventory mappings and existing assessment software can repeat approved calculations with source provenance.
tasks.still_hard: Missing release, fate and disposal evidence can prevent a defensible impact conclusion even when calculations run correctly.
tasks.human_edge: The technician distinguishes a computed scenario from a demonstrated environmental outcome.

ambition.what: Compare an additional product scenario using the same explicit functional unit and source assumptions.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2–5 for supplier data, assessment licences and engineering review

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: life-cycle assessment tools can calculate impacts from a versioned inventory and assessment method; deterministic imports and templates can repeat approved scenarios.

assumptions: This is provisional effort arithmetic, not an observed baseline or an environmental-impact estimate.

Actual material, energy and transport records must already be available with units and provenance. Supplier-data collection and new experiments must be separately counted if required; missing values remain explicit.
OTHER means the organisation's life-cycle assessment application. Existing native import and scenario functions are tested before building mappings.
No model invents nanoscale impact factors or treats an ordinary material factor as validated for a nanomaterial.
The same-system report save has no saving. Overlap with nanomaterial comparison or other inventory tasks must be reconciled at role roll-up rather than added twice.
unknowns: Current native import and reporting features
research_questions: Which inventory mappings need human maintenance?
What uncertainty prevents the intended comparison from being defensible?

already_counted.description: Review the complete report's source support and limitations

incremental.description: Maintain inventory mappings, factor versions and sensitivity checks

approvals.approved_version: approved final life-cycle analysis report; edits require s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 12.5 inventory hours +10 calculation hours +4 report hours =26.5. Three upkeep hours give central net 23.5%; 5.5 extra hours resolving inventory exceptions give high 18%. Low zero if native workflows already cover the work or source gaps prevent reuse.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: nanoengineering supervisor: approve methods and assess uncertain conclusions
laboratory and production owners: provide actual source records
role.ambitious_version: A nanotechnology technician who can repeat traceable comparisons while keeping uncertain environmental claims tied to measured data and explicit assumptions.
